---
title: "Migration notes for app scripts"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Migration notes for app scripts}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

An app script calls blockr.ui 0.0.1 to pick its table preview, which draws the tables that blocks show.
In version 0.2.0, the browser holds the board and draws it, as the migration notes of blockr.core describe (`vignette("migration-notes", package = "blockr.core")`).
The packages of blockr draw their UIs there with the components of blockr.ui.
Nothing of blockr.ui draws in R any more.
So the table preview is gone, and so is every other function of version 0.0.1.

These notes list each change that an app script of blockr.ui 0.0.1 needs to run on blockr.ui 0.2.0.
They are written so that an AI can apply them to a script.
A function of version 0.0.1 that is gone has no alias, so a script that still calls it stops with an error from R.
A script follows the migration notes of blockr.core too, and those of each other blockr package that it calls.

## The table preview

In version 0.0.1, a script picks the table preview of blockr.ui with the blockr option `tabular_display`.
The table preview then draws every table that a block shows:

```r
# blockr.ui 0.0.1
library(blockr.core)

options(blockr.tabular_display = blockr.ui::html_table_display)

serve(new_board(blocks = c(a = new_dataset_block("iris"))))
```

In version 0.2.0, the table preview is gone, and blockr.core reads no blockr option `tabular_display`.
So a script drops the line, and puts nothing in its place:

```r
# blockr.ui 0.2.0
library(blockr.core)

serve(new_board(blocks = c(a = new_dataset_block("iris"))))
```

A call to `options()` may set other options as well.
The script then keeps those, and drops the entry `blockr.tabular_display` alone.

A script that attaches blockr.ui, with `library(blockr.ui)`, may name the table preview without `blockr.ui::`, as `options(blockr.tabular_display = html_table_display)` does.
Such a script drops that line the same way.
Once the script calls nothing of blockr.ui, it drops `library(blockr.ui)` as well.

In version 0.2.0, the plain table of blockr.core draws every table output.
Another package may offer a richer table, as a renderer.
An app draws its tables with such a renderer by naming it in the blockr option `renderers` of blockr.core (see `?blockr.core::new_renderer`).
The package blockr.ui offers no renderer, so a script names none in place of the table preview.

The table preview took the number of rows on each page from the board option `page_size` of blockr.core.
A script that sets that board option, or the blockr option `page_size`, follows the notes of blockr.core, which say what takes their place.

A board that an app saved with the table preview holds nothing of blockr.ui's.
The board option `page_size` that it holds is blockr.core's.
So the file needs only the conversion that the notes of blockr.core describe.

## The functions that go

Version 0.2.0 keeps no function of version 0.0.1.
None of them has a successor in R, since nothing in R draws UI.
So a script that calls one of them drops the call.
The table gives each of them with what does its work in version 0.2.0:

| Version 0.0.1 | Version 0.2.0 |
|---|---|
| `html_table_display` | The plain table of blockr.core, which draws every table output ([The table preview](#the-table-preview)) |
| `html_table_render()`, `html_table_result()`, `table_page()`, `build_html_table()`, `column_widths_px()`, `apply_table_sort()`, `table_preview_dep()` and `table_preview_css()` | Nothing, since the table preview is gone |
| `action_menu()`, `menu_item()`, `menu_section()`, `menu_divider()`, `dropdown()`, `gear_tray()`, `tray_section()`, `shortcut()` and `tool_button()` | Nothing in R, since a package draws its UI in the browser, with the components of blockr.ui |
| `block_mark()`, `block_mark_svg()` and `category_color()` | Nothing in R, since blockr.core draws the mark of each block in the browser, in the colour of its category |
| `small_icon()` | Nothing in R, since blockr.ui offers Lucide's icons to the UIs that packages draw in the browser |
| `theme_dep()`, `controls_dep()` and `base_dep()` | Nothing, since the `serve()` of blockr.core puts the stylesheet of blockr.ui on every page |
| `shiny_has_perf_dep()` and `shiny_input_batch_dep()` | Nothing, since no Shiny input or output draws the board |
